page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Margin notes stand in the right margin. A running head "AULA TIBERIANA." is at the top, with the page number 321 at top right. Nothing is printed at the foot except a gathering mark "X" centred below the text. Dark marks at the left edge belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: spreta exolescunt: si irascare[?], agnita videntur. quod dictum, alta radice cogitationi infigant, qui sibi rem cum convitiatoribus esse noverint. Est aliquis qui teConvitii proterve insultando laesit? aut vince animi magnitu-dinemedela dolorem, aut sensum doloris taciturnitate tege. In judicium provocas? rumorem vulgi pasces. contra-rio convitiandi scripto infectabere? audaciae flammam & causam subjicies, clamore indignabere? va-nam viribus iram vicini ridebunt. Manu & ferro in ul-tionem surges? Virile hoc quidem videtur: sed gravius leviori vulneri remedium. Denique superior læ-dente, existimationi; inferior, tuae saluti nocebis.
main_text.head: Vita ingeniorum à violento inte-ritu.
main_text.p: Quo solamine Cremutius vitam sibi ereptam mitigat. suum cuique decus posteritas rependit. nec deerunt, si damnatio ingruit, qui non modo Cassii & Bruti, sed etiam mei meminerint. Quare prudenter agunt moderatores rerum, nisi modum petulantiae excreverit, si dissimulata offensione, ultione palam igni & ferro jussa, curiosos hominum animos ad inquisitionem talium librorum non accendant. libros per aedilis cremandos censuere patres: sed manserunt occultati, & editi, negligentia fortasse tumulandi, nisi illa flammae luce orbi monstrati fuissent. Quo magis secordiam eorum irridere libet, qui praesenti potentia credunt exstingui posse etiam sequentis aevi memoriam. Nam contrà, pu-nitis ingeniis, glisecit[?] auctoritas. neque aliud externi re-ges, aut qui eadem saevitia usi sunt, nisi dedecus sibi, atque illi gloriam peperere. Rectius rogum & cinerem Fabricii VeientonisVeientis probrosa scripta, in patres & sacerdotes, merebantur. Et tamen quo exustionis eventu? libros exuri jussit, conquisitos lectitatosque donec cum periculo parabantur: mox licentia habendi, oblivionem attulit. xiv.Annal. Optimum vindictæ[?] genus est, vitae integritate scripta in se refutare; inimicos autem scripto laudatos virtute superare.

page.notes: Right margin notes transcribed: "Convitii" (beside "qui te"), "medela" (beside "magnitu-dine"), "Veientis" (beside "Fabricii Veientonis"), "Vindicta" (beside "Optimum vindictae") and "solida[?]" (beside "inimicos"). The note beside "Optimum" was read as "Vindicta" and is written as the next paragraph's note; the last one is doubtful and was not placed in the text. Doubtful readings: "irascare" (first line, blurred), "glisecit" (second half of the line blurred), "vindictæ" (ligature unclear), "solida" (marginal word blurred). The "xiv.Annal." citation at the end of the paragraph is set in the main text, not as a note. Top right marks and left edge marks are not transcribed.
